verdict: Lululemon's revenue rose just 1% to $3.6B in its holiday quarter as China Mainland grew 24% but the Americas shrank, and profit fell 22% to $587M as tariffs and markdowns cut gross margin by 550 points.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: +1% YoY; +6% excluding the 53rd week of fiscal 2024

segments.name: Americas
segments.note: The engine market shrank: revenue fell 4% and comparable sales fell 1% (U.S. revenue -6%, Canada +1%). Excluding the extra 53rd week a year ago, Americas revenue was flat. Still almost three of every four dollars.

segments.name: China Mainland
segments.note: Revenue jumped 24% as reported (21% in constant currency) and comparable sales rose 30% — despite Chinese New Year shifting into the next quarter.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.note: Europe, Asia-Pacific outside mainland China and elsewhere: revenue up 10% as reported, comparable sales up 9%.

flow.costPlain: Making and shipping the clothes — this quarter tariffs and heavier markdowns pushed it up much faster than sales.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Store payroll, marketing and head-office costs — 32.5% of revenue, up from 31.5% a year ago.

opex.name: Amortization of intangible assets
opex.note: Spreading the cost of acquired intangible assets.

takeaways.title: China carried the quarter
takeaways.text: China Mainland revenue rose 24% to $528M with comparable sales up 30%, and Rest of World rose 10% to $432M. The Americas fell 4% to $2,681M — international growth is the only reason total revenue grew at all.

takeaways.title: Margin fell 550 points
takeaways.text: Gross margin dropped to 54.9% from 60.4%: product margin fell 560 points on higher tariffs and heavier markdowns, partly offset by efficiency gains. Operating margin fell to 22.3% from 28.9%.

takeaways.title: Next year's EPS was guided down
takeaways.text: For fiscal 2026 management guided revenue of $11.350–11.500B (up 2–4%) but EPS of $12.10–$12.30, down from $13.26 in fiscal 2025, with Americas revenue expected to fall 1–3%.

oneTimers: Fiscal 2024 had a 53rd week and fiscal 2025 had 52, which distorts every growth rate in this quarter: excluding the extra week, total revenue rose 6% (4% in constant currency) instead of 1%.

Lululemon repurchased 1.4 million of its shares for $269.1M in the quarter and opened 15 net new company-operated stores, ending the year with 811 stores and $1.8B of cash; inventories rose 18% to $1.7B.
otherDetail: Other income, net, was $1.0M, down from $15.4M a year ago on equity-investment write-offs and lower interest income.
footerNote: The release gives only percentage changes by region; the China Mainland ($528.4M) and Rest of World ($431.5M) dollar figures are from Lululemon's Q4 fiscal 2025 financial supplement, with Americas as the residual. Lululemon calls this fiscal year '2025' — it ended February 1, 2026.
